result:
The four packages are scaffolds, so nothing to partition. Here are the outcome candidates from the spec, **unranked**, for you to rank.

## Outcomes

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Spec | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A canonical filing-index catalog in Parquet for a range of archived quarters you choose, built from real SEC `master.idx` files | R1, R3, R5, R11; §4.2 Backfill, §4.4, §4.6 | Full history 1993Q1 to now is about 135 quarterly files, so a few hundred requests including listings: minutes at 3 req/s. Bytes per quarter are a guess (tens of MB from row counts × line length), so the real run measures it. The parser's work for legacy formats can only be measured by running. |
| O2 | Daily indexes added to the catalog, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2, R5; §4.2 Daily | About 250 daily files a year, about one request each plus listings, so seconds per day. The catch-up from the handoff date scales with its length. |
| O3 | Replay: original bytes kept, so a parser change rebuilds the catalog from storage with no new SEC requests | R6; §4.3, §4.5 | Storage roughly equals the raw volume in O1 and O2, plus one copy per changed snapshot. Measured by the run. |
| O4 | Weekly reconciliation: quarterly corrections applied, withdrawals held until you approve them by source hash | R7, R10; §4.4 | Re-fetching all quarters is again a few hundred requests a week. It also costs your time for each withdrawal approval; how often that happens is unknown until it runs. |
| O5 | Readers see only complete, versioned quarter generations through one active pointer, never partial files | R9; §4.5, §4.6 | Small compute. Storage grows with retained generations under a retention policy not yet chosen. |
| O6 | All SEC traffic from the application shares one request budget (3 req/s, an identifying User-Agent), however many workers run | R8, R11; §4.3 | Published ceiling is 10 req/s per user; the target is 3. |
| O7 | The system running on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, managed identities, triggers enabled after catch-up | R4; §4.1, §4.8, §4.9, §7 | Dollars per month can't be estimated until region, job sizes and retention are chosen; a real deployment measures it. |
| O8 | Run reports and alerts showing pending, failed and quarantined sources and gaps, not just a max filing date | §4.7 (no R) | Small. Log Analytics ingestion is billed and is measured with O7. |

R5 (shared code) and R11 (stated defaults) are constraints, not outcomes. They are cited in the Spec cells of the outcomes they bind.

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: source manifest, provenance traceability, full validation suite, runbooks.

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Filing-index catalog** (O1–O6). Known progression: the spec fully determines its method.
- **B: Azure operation** (O7, O8). Known progression, following the spec's §7 phases.
  - **Why split:** a correct catalog stands without Azure, since it runs locally against real SEC files. Azure hosting answers a separate question (how it runs unattended), and the ADR is still *Proposed*, with a schedule-only container option in §9.
  - Joined, the catalog would wait on ADF, identities and infrastructure-as-code.
  - The Storage-backed lease in O6 is the one point where A meets B.
  - If you consider the ADR still open, B becomes a research track.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv workspace.
- Code lives in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (§4.9). The other three scaffolds (`-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`) aren't named by the spec. I'll treat them as unassigned unless you say otherwise.
- Azure platform per the ADR (Proposed, 2026-10-05).

The roadmap file will be `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md` (the spec's stem).

Optionally, I can fetch one real quarterly `master.idx` and one daily index to replace the size guesses with measured figures. I'll do this only if you say yes.

**Your call:** rank the outcomes within each track and the two tracks against each other, and confirm or change the tracks and their kinds.
